claims.claim: Origen was born probably at Alexandria in 184/85 and died probably in Tyre in 253/54 after imprisonment and torture during the Decian persecution.
Origen was the son of the martyr Leonides and was the oldest in a family of seven children.
Origen was an outstanding theologian of the early Greek-speaking Church.

Origen's chief aim was to be an interpreter of the Scriptures, and to this end he composed scientific commentaries on various books of the Old and New Testaments, homilies, and short exegetical notes.

The Homilies on Genesis and Exodus belong to the category of homilies, and though Origen did not reject the literal sense of Scripture, he is more intent upon the spiritual meanings of passages selected from Genesis and Exodus.
The English translation was made from the surviving Latin translation of Rufinus of Aquileia.
The work includes Greek fragments of the Homilies on Genesis and Exodus.
The work has a Latin manuscript tradition with editions and translations.
Origen was a pupil of Clement of Alexandria, whom he succeeded as head of the Catechetical school under the authority of the bishop Demetrius.
Origen founded the Christian School of Caesarea, where he taught logic, cosmology, natural history, and theology.
